title: Ramses II and the Hittites: the first written peace treaty
summary: Ramses II and the Hittites: the first written peace treaty
description: Record first created by the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)). CFAH dates it as well (added by the CFAH pass); the sort follows the four-tier rule.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 1: CFAH anchor point: 624/623 BC (AP-73, OSF preprint CFAH-9). Sort changed by the CFAH pass (2026-10-18): was provisional (Generations) 1279 BC.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "CFAH-9: The 19th and 26th Dynasties of Egypt," OSF preprint v1.4 (25 Sep 2025), doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/HV3B2, file CFAH-9_Dynasties_19_and_26_v1.4.pdf, p. 29, section "AP-73: Treaty of Kadesh, 624/623 BC"
chronologies.note: CFAH-9 elsewhere gives the treaty year as 623 BC (see open question I13). CFAH's revised chronology places Rameses II in the 7th century BC, so this moves the record far from its conventional (Generations) date.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 10 "The Assyrian Empire: Power by Cruelty (1200–612 BC)", PDF p. 298 (printed p. 297)
chronologies.note: Ramses II conquers the Hittite kingdom; the first significant written peace treaty.
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); not in 2nd ed. (2024): no dated statement for this was found in the 2nd ed. (2024).

free_source_links.locator: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)
